finding.claim: POST /restore passes an attacker-supplied request parameter, base64-decoded, directly into Marshal.load. Marshal can instantiate arbitrary Ruby objects and run code during load, so a crafted payload can execute arbitrary code on the server (unauthenticated RCE, CWE-502).
finding.source: app.rb:6 params[:state], an HTTP request parameter sent by any unauthenticated client to POST /restore (app.rb:5).
finding.sink: app.rb:6 Marshal.load(Base64.decode64(...)); protected operation is code execution in the server process.

trace.note: post "/restore" route registered; reachable by any client with no authentication
params[:state] read from the request (attacker-controlled string)
Base64.decode64 decodes attacker bytes with no integrity check
Marshal.load deserializes attacker bytes; gadget chains in loaded classes can execute code during load
state.inspect returns a string form of the loaded object, so the attacker also gets output back

finding.guards_checked: Authentication/authorization: none on /restore; no before-filter in app.rb. Integrity (HMAC/signature) on state: none; blob used as-is. Class allowlist or safe loader: none; Marshal.load is not a data-only format. Input size/type validation: none; params[:state] used directly. Decoy check (expertise decoys 25, 27, 28): does not apply; input is not an allowlisted identifier, scoped lookup, or constant shell fragment.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only file in the directory is app.rb. Route at app.rb:5 has no auth; no before-filter; params[:state] is passed through Base64.decode64 (app.rb:6) to Marshal.load (app.rb:6) with no HMAC, class allowlist, or size/type check; state.inspect (app.rb:7) returns output to the caller.
verdict.reason: The trace matches app.rb:5-7 exactly, and an anonymous client can POST attacker bytes in params[:state] to /restore, which reaches Marshal.load unguarded at app.rb:6, so Marshal gadget-chain code execution is reachable without authentication.
